transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose what brought me in is... it's mostly about what happens after my evening class. I've been taking this continuing education course for accounting software at the community college. Just trying to keep up, you know? The younger clerks at the firm are so quick with the new systems, and I really don't want to get left behind or replaced by someone fresh out of high school. It's just a couple of nights a week, but the parking over there is an absolute nightmare. 

But anyway, what I meant to say was, after class gets out, I sometimes stop for food and... I just end up eating a whole fast-food meal. And then I'll grab candy from the vending machine in the lobby—they still have those old spiral ones that always jam, but I usually manage to get something out—and then I get home and just eat even more snacks. It's like I'm making up for the whole day all at once. My wife is usually asleep by then, but I'll just be standing there in the kitchen...
Do you feel like you lose control when you're eating all of that, or like you can't stop once you start?

Yeah, I guess... it really is like that. Once I start on those snacks, I keep telling myself to just close the bag and go to bed. I usually buy those sourdough pretzels, the big thick ones? My wife Susan actually hates them because of the salt crumbs. She's incredibly particular about the kitchen floor. We put in this luxury vinyl plank a few years ago—looks exactly like oak, but way cheaper and you don't have to worry about water damage if the dishwasher leaks. The contractor did a terrible job on the baseboards, though, left these huge gaps that drive me crazy every time I look down at them... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. The eating. I'll be standing there on that floor, and I tell myself to just put the chip clip on the bag, but my hands just... they keep reaching in for more. It's like I'm on autopilot. I just keep going and going until I feel completely embarrassed and, honestly, sick of myself.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or do anything else to try to get rid of the calories you consumed?

Well, a few times, yeah. I mean, after those late-night eating spells, I have gone into the bathroom and made myself throw up. I just get so scared that all that food is going to show on me, you know? My waistline is already expanding, and I had to buy these new slacks for work. I usually go to this department store at the mall—the one that's anchoring the east end? But honestly, the mall is a ghost town these days. Half the stores are boarded up, and the food court is just depressing. They used to have this fantastic pretzel place, not the sourdough kind, but the soft, buttery ones. Now it's just a sad-looking pizza stand and a place that sells those weird bubble teas. I tried one once, and those little tapioca balls are just a choking hazard if you ask me. Susan loves them, though. She goes with her sister on Saturdays... 

But yeah, anyway, the throwing up. It's not every time, but a few times I've just felt so full and guilty that I went to the bathroom and did it. I just couldn't stand the thought of all those calories just sitting there.
How often would you say you have these episodes where you feel like you're eating a lot of food in a short amount of time and can't stop yourself?

Well, I'd say it's been going on for about the past three months or so. Usually, it's at least one night a week, always after that evening class. I mean, the class is only on Tuesdays and Thursdays, but by the time we finish the modules on accounts receivable—which, honestly, they overcomplicate in the new software. The old version we used back in 2015 was so much more intuitive. You just hit F4 and it populated the whole ledger. Now you have to click through three different drop-down menus, and half the time the server lags because the community college's Wi-Fi is practically dial-up speed. The instructor, Mr. Henderson, he tries his best, but he's got this habit of jingling the change in his pocket the whole two hours. It drives me absolutely up the wall. I sit in the second row, right by the window, and the radiator there clanks every twenty minutes... 

But, uh, what was I saying? Oh, right, the frequency. Yeah, so for the last three months, it's been about once a week where I just completely overdo it with the food after class, and then... well, then I go and make myself throw up afterward. It's just that one night a week usually, but it's been pretty consistent lately.
Do these episodes and the way you deal with them afterward cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Well, it definitely bothers me, yeah. I mean, I still get my bookkeeping work done, and I'm keeping up with the coursework for the most part. But lately... I don't know, I just feel this heavy sense of shame about the whole thing. I've actually started packing up my bag before Mr. Henderson even finishes his wrap-up. I just want to get out of there as fast as possible. I used to stick around and chat with a couple of the other folks in the class—there's this guy, Gary, who works over at the auto parts store on Route 9. He's always got these crazy stories about customers trying to return used brake pads. And he drives this immaculate 1978 Ford F-150. Two-tone, brown and tan. You just don't see trucks in that kind of condition anymore, especially with the salt they put on the roads around here in the winter. It eats right through the undercarriage. I always tell my wife we need to get the car washed more often in January, but the line at the Delta Sonic is always backed up all the way to the street...

But anyway, yeah, I don't really talk to Gary or anyone else after class anymore. I just duck out and head straight to my car. I'm just so preoccupied with getting home and... well, you know. It's just always on my mind, and I feel too embarrassed to be around people when I'm feeling like that.
Besides making yourself vomit, do you ever go to extreme lengths to burn off the calories you consumed—like exercising for a really long time, fasting, or taking diet pills or laxatives?

No, no, I don't do any of that other stuff. I mean, I don't exercise at all, really. My wife bought me one of those stationary bikes a couple of years ago—the ones with the screen where the instructor yells at you? We put it down in the basement, right next to the old chest freezer. That freezer has been running since 1998, never missed a beat. It's a Kenmore, back when they actually built things to last. We keep half a cow in there that we buy from a local farmer, Jim. Jim's a good guy, raises Black Angus. He used to be a volunteer firefighter with my brother-in-law, Dave. Dave just retired last month, actually. They threw him a huge party at the VFW hall. Had this incredible spread—pulled pork, baked beans, coleslaw. The coleslaw had a little too much vinegar for my taste, but everyone else seemed to love it... 

But, uh, no, I don't take pills or fast or anything like that. Just the throwing up, like I mentioned. The bike in the basement is basically just a very expensive coat rack at this point.
When you're having these episodes of eating a lot and feeling out of control, do you feel like they're related to how you see your body or your weight?

Yeah, I suppose it is. It's just... well, on days my shirt feels tight around my middle, I just feel terrible. Speaking of shirts, I usually get my button-downs from this place over in the strip mall, Miller's Menswear. Old man Miller used to run it, but his son, Todd, took over a few years back. Todd doesn't know the first thing about tailoring, honestly. I brought in a pair of slacks to get hemmed last month for my niece's wedding, and they came back a full inch too short. You could see my socks! And I only wear those Gold Toe socks, you know the ones with the reinforced toe? They last forever. I bought a pack of six at the outlet mall back in 2018 and they still don't have a single hole in them. They're a cotton-poly blend, which is really the way to go if you don't want them shrinking in the dryer. My wife insists on drying everything on high heat, which I keep telling her is going to ruin the elastic in the waistbands... 

But, um, sorry, what was I saying? Right, the weight thing. Yeah, when my shirt feels tight like that, I just feel like I have completely failed. I try to be this careful, disciplined person, you know? And when the clothes don't fit right, I feel like I've lost all that discipline, even if the rest of my bookkeeping work is totally fine and my ledgers are perfectly balanced for the day. It just really gets to me.
Do you judge yourself harshly based on your body shape or weight, like feeling that your value as a person depends on how you look or how much you weigh?

Well, yeah, I guess I kind of already said that, but yes. It's like... if my shirt is tight around my middle, I just feel this overwhelming sense that I've completely failed. Like I've lost all my discipline. And I pride myself on being a careful, disciplined guy. I mean, my ledgers at work are always perfect, to the penny. Speaking of work, my boss, Mr. Abernathy, just bought this massive new mahogany desk for his office. Must weigh three hundred pounds. It took four guys from the delivery company to get it up the stairs, and one of them scuffed the drywall right near the breakroom. The maintenance guy, Carl, was furious. Carl takes his drywall patching very seriously. He uses this quick-setting compound that dries in like twenty minutes, but you have to mix it just right or it gets all lumpy. He showed me how to do it once when I was fixing a hole in my garage where my son backed his bike into the wall... 

But anyway, yeah, the weight thing. Even if my bookkeeping is flawless and everything else is going fine, if the clothes don't fit right, I just feel like a total failure as a person. It's hard to shake that feeling.
Would you say that your overall sense of self-worth is dominated by how you feel about your body shape or weight?

Well, I don't know if "dominated" is the right word. I mean, it's definitely a big part of it, like I was saying. But I have other things I care about, you know? Like my garden. I spend a lot of time out there in the spring. I've got these heirloom tomatoes I've been growing from seeds I save every year. It's a tricky process, saving seeds. You have to let the tomato get almost overripe, then scoop out the seeds and let them ferment in a jar of water for a few days to get that gel coating off. If you don't do that, they won't germinate properly. I learned that from this gardening show on PBS. The host, he's this British fellow with a really soothing voice, he always says you have to be patient with nature. He's got this amazing greenhouse in the English countryside, all glass and wrought iron. I'd love to have a greenhouse like that, but our zoning laws in the township are a nightmare. My neighbor, Phil, tried to put up a little plastic hoop house last year and the zoning board made him tear it down because it was two feet too close to the property line. Phil was so mad he didn't speak to anyone on the board for six months. He even stopped going to the rotary club meetings...

But, uh, what was the question? Oh, right, my self-worth. I don't know, I guess it's a mix. The weight bothers me a lot, sure, but I don't think it's the *only* thing that matters to me. I've got the bookkeeping, the garden... so, no, I wouldn't say it totally dominates everything. Just, you know, it ruins my day when the clothes don't fit.
Would you say that your body shape or weight has a stronger impact on how you feel about yourself than other aspects of your life, like your work or relationships?

Well, I think I've kind of touched on that already, haven't I? It's just... yes, it has a huge impact. Like I was saying before, if I put on a shirt and it's tight around my middle, it just wrecks me. I feel like I've completely failed at being the careful, disciplined person I try to be. Even if my bookkeeping work is perfectly fine that day. Speaking of the bookkeeping, we use this software, QuickLedger Pro, and they just pushed out an update last Tuesday that completely changed the user interface. It's a disaster. The icons are all moved around, and they changed the color scheme to this awful neon green and dark grey. It's supposed to be "modern," but it just gives me a headache. My coworker, Brenda, she called tech support about it and was on hold for forty-five minutes. Forty-five minutes! And when she finally got someone, it was this guy who sounded like he was eating a sandwich the whole time. You could hear him chewing! I mean, the lack of professionalism these days is just astounding. Back when I started in this field, you wore a tie to the office and you certainly didn't eat while on a business call. People had standards. My father always told me... 

Oh, right, sorry. You were asking about the weight thing compared to other stuff. Yeah, it's just... even if I do a great job at work, if that shirt is tight, all I can think about is how I've lost my discipline. It just overshadows the good stuff, you know?
Would you say that your perception of your body weight or shape has an unusually strong influence on how you judge your overall self-worth?

Doc, I feel like we're going in circles a bit here. Like I've been saying, yes, I guess you could call it an unusually strong influence. If I wake up and my work shirt is feeling tight around my middle, I just feel like I've completely failed at being the careful, disciplined guy I try to be. It just ruins my mindset, even if the rest of my bookkeeping work that day is absolutely perfect. 

Speaking of my work shirts, I actually had to switch dry cleaners recently because of that. Well, not because of the weight, but I used to go to Martin's on 4th Street. Martin retired a few months ago and his son took over the shop. The kid uses way too much starch. I told him, look, I sit at a desk crunching numbers all day, I don't need my collar feeling like a piece of cardboard. But young people just don't listen to feedback anymore. My nephew, Jimmy, he's exactly the same way. He just bought this used Honda Civic and the very first thing he did was put one of those ridiculous, loud mufflers on it. I told him he's just going to wake up his whole street when he leaves for his morning shift at the hardware store, but he just rolled his eyes at me. You know, when I was his age, if an older person gave you practical advice, you actually took it to heart. We had respect for our elders. But Jimmy... 

Wait, what were we just talking about? Oh, the self-worth thing. Yeah, so, like I said, if the shirt is tight, I just feel like a total failure.

Would you say that your evaluation of yourself—whether you feel good about who you are—depends so much on your body shape or weight that it overshadows most other qualities or accomplishments you have?

Doc, are you testing my memory here? Because I swear you're just asking me the exact same question again. 

It's just like I keep telling you—yes, it completely overshadows things. If I put on my work shirt and it's tight around my middle, all I can think is that I've lost all my discipline. I feel like a total failure for not being the careful person I try to be. It ruins my whole mindset, even if I go to the office and my bookkeeping work is absolutely fine that day. 

And honestly, my bookkeeping is more than fine, even when I have to deal with the most ridiculous clients. Just yesterday, this guy brings in his quarterly expenses in a shoebox. An actual cardboard shoebox! And not even a nice one, it was from a pair of cheap discount sneakers. He just dumps these crumpled receipts on my desk, and half of them are faded because they're printed on that cheap thermal paper. I keep telling people, if you leave thermal paper in a hot truck, it turns completely black! You can't read a single number on it! I had to hold one receipt up to the window like some kind of detective just to see if he bought PVC pipes or a coffee maker. You'd think a guy running a plumbing business would know how to use a basic manila folder. My uncle Arthur was a plumber, actually. Started his own business back in '78. He had this old Ford van, kept it spotless. He always said your vehicle is your moving billboard, so if it's dirty, people think your work is dirty. He used to wash it every Sunday afternoon in his driveway...

But, uh, anyway. I feel like a broken record here, but yeah. If the weight is up and the clothes don't fit, it just makes me feel like I failed, no matter how good I am at my job. I think we've pretty much covered that, haven't we?

Would you say that how you see your body shape or weight is the main thing that determines how you feel about yourself as a person, even more than other things like your skills, accomplishments, or relationships?

Doc, are you pulling my leg? Is this a trick question? Because I swear, this is the fourth time you've asked me the exact same thing in a different way. 

Yes, it is the main thing. Like I keep saying, if I put on my shirt in the morning and it's tight around my middle, it just completely ruins me. I feel like I've totally failed at being the careful, disciplined guy I'm supposed to be. And it doesn't matter if I go to work and balance the books perfectly for the rest of the day, that feeling just hangs over me. 

Speaking of the books, I finally got that shoebox guy's accounts sorted out. Took me three hours just to decipher his gas receipts. And you know what the worst part is? Gas prices right now. I went to fill up my sedan on Tuesday, and the station on the corner of Elm and 5th—the one that used to be a Texaco but is now some independent place called "Star Gas" or something—they jacked up their prices by fifteen cents overnight! Fifteen cents! I asked the kid behind the counter about it, and he just shrugged and went back to looking at his phone. Nobody cares about customer service anymore. I remember when they used to pump the gas for you and check your oil. Now you're lucky if they even make eye contact when you hand them your credit card. I mean, my first job was at a grocery store, bagging items, and Mr. Henderson, the manager, he made sure we looked every single customer in the eye and said "Thank you, have a good day." If you didn't, he'd have you sweeping the stockroom for a week...

But anyway, yeah. The weight thing. If the shirt is tight, I feel like a failure, no matter what else I accomplish. Can we please move on to a different question now?
Would you say that your perception of your body weight or shape has an unusually strong influence on how you judge your overall self-worth?

Doc, are we... are we seriously doing this again? I feel like I'm losing my mind here. You've literally asked me this exact same thing, what, five times now? 

I don't know how else to say it. Yes. If I wake up, put on my button-down, and it's tight around my middle, I feel like I've completely failed. I feel like I've lost all the discipline I'm supposed to have. It just wrecks me, and it doesn't matter if I go to the office and my bookkeeping is completely perfect all day long. 

Speaking of the office, they just changed the brand of coffee in the breakroom. Used to be Folgers. Classic, reliable, gets the job done. Now it's some fancy, fair-trade, organic dark roast that tastes like burnt dirt. I swear, the office manager, Susan, she just buys whatever has the prettiest packaging. And she bought these new mugs, too—they don't even have handles! Who buys a coffee mug without a handle? You just burn your hands trying to hold the thing. I tried to bring in my own mug from home, the one my sister got me from her trip to the Grand Canyon back in '04, but someone knocked it off the drying rack and chipped the rim. I was furious. I told Susan she needs to implement a strict "you break it, you buy it" policy for the breakroom, but she just laughed it off. Nobody respects personal property anymore. It's just like my neighbor, leaving his garbage cans out for three days after pickup...

But, look, I don't know what else you want me to tell you about the weight thing. If the shirt is tight, I feel like a failure. Can we please, for the love of Pete, talk about something else now?

Would you say that how you see your body shape or weight is the main thing that determines how you feel about yourself as a person, even more than other things like your skills, accomplishments, or relationships?

Doc... are you feeling okay? Because I think your record is skipping. You literally just asked me that exact same question. Is this some kind of psychological stress test? 

I really, truly don't know how many different ways I can explain this to you. Yes. If I button up my work shirt and it's pulling tight across my middle, my whole day is shot. I feel like I've completely failed at being the careful, disciplined guy I try to be. And it doesn't matter one bit if I go in and my bookkeeping work is absolutely flawless all day. 

And it *has* been flawless, by the way, despite the fact that someone keeps stealing my good pens. I buy these specific gel pens—Pilot G2s, 0.7 millimeter, black ink. I buy them with my own money because the ones Susan orders for the supply closet are those cheap ballpoints that skip and leave ink blobs all over the ledgers. You can't have ink blobs on a financial report! It looks completely unprofessional. Anyway, I keep my G2s in a little mug on my desk, and I swear, every time I come back from the restroom, one is missing. I think it's Dave from sales. He always walks by my desk pretending to look at the quarterly projections, but I know he's eyeing my pens. I even tried putting a little piece of red tape on the caps so I could identify them if I saw them on his desk, but my wife told me I was being paranoid. She says I shouldn't care so much about office supplies, but when you work with numbers all day, precision matters. Just like my dad used to say, measure twice, cut once. He was a carpenter, you know, built half the houses in our old neighborhood...

But, uh, anyway. The shirt thing. If it's tight, I feel like a failure. That's the bottom line. Can we please, please move on to the next question on your notepad?
